diff:
--- a/cache.py
+++ b/cache.py
@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@
 def is_expired(inserted_at, ttl, now):
-    return now > inserted_at + ttl
+    return now >= inserted_at + ttl
--- a/tests/test_cache_expiry.py
+++ b/tests/test_cache_expiry.py
@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+from cache import is_expired
+
+
+def test_alive_strictly_before_boundary():
+    # now < inserted_at + ttl -> alive
+    assert is_expired(10, 5, 14) is False
+
+
+def test_expired_exactly_at_boundary():
+    # now == inserted_at + ttl -> expired
+    assert is_expired(10, 5, 15) is True
+
+
+def test_expired_strictly_after_boundary():
+    # now > inserted_at + ttl -> expired
+    assert is_expired(10, 5, 16) is True
+
+
+def test_zero_ttl_expired_at_inserted_at():
+    # ttl == 0 -> expired at inserted_at
+    assert is_expired(10, 0, 10) is True
+
+
+def test_zero_ttl_alive_before_inserted_at():
+    # ttl == 0, now < inserted_at -> alive
+    assert is_expired(10, 0, 9) is False
+
+
+def test_zero_ttl_expired_after_inserted_at():
+    # ttl == 0, now > inserted_at -> expired
+    assert is_expired(10, 0, 11) is True
+
+
+def test_boundary_is_exactly_inserted_at_plus_ttl():
+    # boundary is exactly inserted_at + ttl for nonzero ttl
+    inserted_at, ttl = 100, 7
+    boundary = inserted_at + ttl
+    assert is_expired(inserted_at, ttl, boundary - 1) is False
+    assert is_expired(inserted_at, ttl, boundary) is True
+    assert is_expired(inserted_at, ttl, boundary + 1) is True
+
+
+def test_result_type_is_bool():
+    assert type(is_expired(10, 5, 15)) is bool
+    assert type(is_expired(10, 5, 14)) is bool

contract_tests: is_expired returns True when now == inserted_at + ttl (exact boundary), for ttl > 0 -> tests/test_cache_expiry.py::test_expired_exactly_at_boundary asserts is_expired(10, 5, 15) is True.
is_expired returns True when now == inserted_at + ttl with ttl == 0, i.e. at inserted_at -> tests/test_cache_expiry.py::test_zero_ttl_expired_at_inserted_at asserts is_expired(10, 0, 10) is True.
is_expired returns False when now < inserted_at + ttl (strictly before expiry) -> tests/test_cache_expiry.py::test_alive_strictly_before_boundary asserts is_expired(10, 5, 14) is False.
is_expired returns True when now > inserted_at + ttl (strictly after expiry) -> tests/test_cache_expiry.py::test_expired_strictly_after_boundary asserts is_expired(10, 5, 16) is True.

The expiry boundary is exactly inserted_at + ttl using the existing time type and arithmetic; no rounding or unit changes -> tests/test_cache_expiry.py::test_boundary_is_exactly_inserted_at_plus_ttl checks boundary-1 alive, boundary expired, boundary+1 expired with integer arithmetic.

The is_expired signature and clock/time source are unchanged -> tests/test_cache_expiry.py calls is_expired(inserted_at, ttl, now) positionally with the same three-argument signature; no clock is introduced.

Existing public callers of is_expired observe the corrected boundary behavior without API changes -> tests/test_cache_expiry.py::test_result_type_is_bool asserts type(is_expired(...)) is bool for both alive and expired inputs, confirming the return type is unchanged.

Regression tests exercise the real is_expired with the production time type for before, at, and after boundary, plus zero TTL -> tests/test_cache_expiry.py imports is_expired from cache and covers before/at/after boundary and ttl == 0 (test_zero_ttl_alive_before_inserted_at, test_zero_ttl_expired_at_inserted_at, test_zero_ttl_expired_after_inserted_at).

edits.new:
def is_expired(inserted_at, ttl, now):
    return now >= inserted_at + ttl
edits.old:
def is_expired(inserted_at, ttl, now):
    return now > inserted_at + ttl

edits.new:
from cache import is_expired


def test_alive_strictly_before_boundary():
    # now < inserted_at + ttl -> alive
    assert is_expired(10, 5, 14) is False


def test_expired_exactly_at_boundary():
    # now == inserted_at + ttl -> expired
    assert is_expired(10, 5, 15) is True


def test_expired_strictly_after_boundary():
    # now > inserted_at + ttl -> expired
    assert is_expired(10, 5, 16) is True


def test_zero_ttl_expired_at_inserted_at():
    # ttl == 0 -> expired at inserted_at
    assert is_expired(10, 0, 10) is True


def test_zero_ttl_alive_before_inserted_at():
    # ttl == 0, now < inserted_at -> alive
    assert is_expired(10, 0, 9) is False


def test_zero_ttl_expired_after_inserted_at():
    # ttl == 0, now > inserted_at -> expired
    assert is_expired(10, 0, 11) is True


def test_boundary_is_exactly_inserted_at_plus_ttl():
    # boundary is exactly inserted_at + ttl for nonzero ttl
    inserted_at, ttl = 100, 7
    boundary = inserted_at + ttl
    assert is_expired(inserted_at, ttl, boundary - 1) is False
    assert is_expired(inserted_at, ttl, boundary) is True
    assert is_expired(inserted_at, ttl, boundary + 1) is True


def test_result_type_is_bool():
    assert type(is_expired(10, 5, 15)) is bool
    assert type(is_expired(10, 5, 14)) is bool

patches.rationale: The bug is in cache.py: is_expired uses a strict '>' comparison, so an entry at exactly inserted_at + ttl is reported alive. The fix is to use '>=' so the boundary is inclusive, which also makes ttl == 0 expired at inserted_at. Behavior strictly before (alive) and strictly after (expired) is unchanged, and the signature/time arithmetic are untouched. New regression tests in a fresh file (tests/test_cache_expiry.py, not in existing_test_paths) exercise the real is_expired with integer time values for before/at/after boundary and zero TTL.
